title: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

scenes.purpose: Show the viewer the record's two endpoints before the conclusion is drawn from them.

visual.description: Dark field; two stat tiles settle side by side, '10 s · 1972' on the left and '37 s · 2017' on the right; a thin line connects them, rising in one direction only, standing in for the table's other steps between them.

chart.title: TAI-UTC, first value to latest
chart.note: These tiles mark the table's first and last values only; the rows between them each rise by exactly one second. Don't imply a smooth or constant rate between 1972 and 2017, and don't draw the other 26 steps as a curve.

scenes.direction: Hard cut in; the two tiles and the connecting line settle together; hold briefly on the line's single upward direction.
scenes.narration: The IERS table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds to 37 seconds, each entry a second larger than the last.

scenes.purpose: State the conclusion the record supports: every step in the table added a second, none subtracted one.

visual.description: Dark field; the line 'None has ever been taken away' types on in large serif, centred; 'taken away' holds and turns to the accent glow as the sentence ends.
onScreenText: None has ever been taken away.

scenes.direction: Hard cut from the tiles; the line types on word by word; hold on the settled statement before the close card.
scenes.narration: That means every leap second has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away.
